result.summary: The main visual defect is horizontal content overflow: the category row and the "Fastest near you" restaurant carousel are clipped at the right edge, making items look cut off. The rest of the page is generally coherent, though the lower content is naturally obscured by the fixed bottom navigation.

issues.description: The horizontal category-chip row overflows the viewport; a partial chip is visibly cut off along the right edge with no clear inset or affordance that the row can scroll.
issues.suggestion: Implement the category list as an intentional horizontally scrollable container with consistent side padding and optional visual scroll affordance, ensuring chips are not awkwardly clipped.

issues.description: The third card in the "Fastest near you" carousel is cut off by the right screen boundary, including its image, restaurant name ("Trattoria Piccol..."), and delivery text. This makes the content appear truncated rather than deliberately scrollable.
issues.suggestion: Use a properly padded horizontal carousel with fixed card widths and a visible partial-next-card cue, or resize cards so the intended number of cards fits cleanly within the viewport.

issues.description: The "Popular right now" list continues underneath the fixed bottom navigation, so the next restaurant card is partially hidden at the bottom of the screen.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom content padding equal to or greater than the fixed navigation height so the final list items can be fully viewed and interacted with when scrolled.
